s: No one thought James would appear at Katie's party.  So when he ______, everyone was surprised and could not believe their eyes.【104年會考】
e: 用簡答句描述一件過去的事情，代替前面的動詞appear，要用過去式的助動詞did，故選(Ｄ)。

s: Actor David Piper became tired of talking about the movie ______ after he was interviewed about it many times.【104年會考】
e: 先行詞是the movie，將the movie帶進關係子句中還原為that he is famous for the movie，本題關係代名詞是受格，可省略that，故選(Ｄ)。

中譯：獵捕新聞
Kieran Hardy 11/07/2013
　　多年來我們都認為我們的地球是唯一的藍色星球。現在已經發現另外一個了。它的名字是HD189773b。HD189773b是一個系外行星，位於太陽系之外，也是離地球最近的系外行星之一。即便如此，我們也不能稱之為鄰居，原因如下：它距離地球63光年遠；意思就是離我們有370,440,000,000,000英里遠。即使我們以一小時3,500英里的速度飛行，我們也要花一百二十萬年才能到達那裡。
　　除了它的顏色是藍的以外，HD189773b再也沒有跟我們星球相像的地方了。它比地球大很多，是由氣體所組成的，而且相當炙熱。熱度高達攝氏一千度，這樣是不可能有任何生命存在的。更糟的是，它會像下雨一樣的下「玻璃」。如果攝氏一千度殺不死你，「玻璃雨」也會殺死你。
　　即便如此，找到這個藍色巨物仍給了我們希望。這是第一次我們可以看到一個系外行星的顏色。這個星球的顏色，讓我們知道星球上面發生了什麼事。當我們處於在找尋一個可以居住的新星球的漫長路途中，找到一個藍色的星球是一個好的開始。

中譯：　　這是Nick Foster新書—《與食物結婚》的前言。
前言
　　我媽媽不擅長做飯。對她來說，做菜比較像是一個令人興奮的實驗。你把這些和那些東西放到鍋子裡，然後等著看會發生什麼事。當她的實驗最後結果不好的時候，她會說：「沒有經過實驗，就不會有經驗。」，而我聽過很多次了。
　　我的爸爸是一個厲害的廚師，而他也很愛做菜。他是用一桌好菜才讓我媽媽嫁給他的，而不是用一枚美麗的戒指。他說：「一個家庭裡只要有一個人會做菜就可以了。」
　　現在我自己就是個廚師。我擁有自己的餐廳。當然我是跟我爸爸學做菜的。從他那裡，我學到了做菜的藝術。但是我從我媽媽那兒還是學到了一件事，就是她的名言：「沒有經過實驗，就不會有經驗。」

s: (１)What does The idea mean in the reading?
p:
The idea may hit you once or twice a year. You come home on a hot summer day, hoping to have a cool bath, and find out there is no water. Then you see how important water is in your everyday life. However, in many parts of the world, water is not just about one's everyday needs.
　　In countries like Tanzania, water is hard to get, and the job of collecting water falls on women's shoulders. Girls are often kept home from school to collect water while their brothers stay at school studying. Studies show Tanzanian girls who live 15 minutes from clean water spend 12％ more time at school than those who live an hour away. More time spent collecting water means less time for learning. For these girls,“Knowledge is power”is not just words; it is a sad fact in real life. With less time spent at school, their chances of getting well-paid jobs are small, and they often have no voice in important matters, like who to marry. These girls are often married into poor families. They have little money or knowledge to take care of their children, who often end up dying young. For the baby girls who are lucky enough to live, their life may still center around“water,”just like it did for their mothers.
【104年會考】

e: 因為女孩要去取水，不能進學校讀書，長大以後找不到較好的工作，也比較沒有地位，沒有發言權，故選(Ｂ)。

s: (４)Families in the countries of Benin, Ghana, Guinea and Madagascar deal with the job of water-collecting the same way Tanzanian families do. From the reading, which chart best shows the fact?
p:
The idea may hit you once or twice a year. You come home on a hot summer day, hoping to have a cool bath, and find out there is no water. Then you see how important water is in your everyday life. However, in many parts of the world, water is not just about one's everyday needs.
　　In countries like Tanzania, water is hard to get, and the job of collecting water falls on women's shoulders. Girls are often kept home from school to collect water while their brothers stay at school studying. Studies show Tanzanian girls who live 15 minutes from clean water spend 12％ more time at school than those who live an hour away. More time spent collecting water means less time for learning. For these girls,“Knowledge is power”is not just words; it is a sad fact in real life. With less time spent at school, their chances of getting well-paid jobs are small, and they often have no voice in important matters, like who to marry. These girls are often married into poor families. They have little money or knowledge to take care of their children, who often end up dying young. For the baby girls who are lucky enough to live, their life may still center around“water,”just like it did for their mothers.
【104年會考】
e:
由文中內容可知，取水的工作都落在女孩的身上，圖表中找水所花費的時間應為女生多於男生，故選(Ｄ)。
中譯：　　這個想法可能一年內你會想到一至兩次。你在一個炎熱的夏日回家，希望洗個冷水澡，但卻發現沒有水。於是你會發現在日常生活中水有多重要。然而，在世界的很多地區，水不只是每個人的日常所需而已。
　　像是在坦尚尼亞，水很難取得，取水的工作落在女性的肩膀上。女孩們常常得為了取水留在家裡不去學校，然而她們的兄弟們還待在學校上課。研究顯示，在坦尚尼亞，住在離水源15分鐘遠的女孩，比住在離水源一小時遠的女孩可多出12％的時間在學校。花越多的時間在取水上，意謂著學習的時間越少。對這些女孩來說，「知識就是力量」不只是文字，而是真實人生中的一個悲慘事實。隨著在學校的時間越少，她們能得到好工作的機會就越小，而且她們也常常對於重要事件沒有發言權，例如要嫁給誰。這些女孩常常嫁入窮人家。她們幾乎沒有錢和知識去照顧她們的小孩，導致小孩早夭。幸運能活下來的女嬰，她們的生活依然圍繞著「水」為中心，如同她們母親以前的生活一樣。

s: (１)What is Garden House?
p:
(At Liz's birthday party)
Amber: Don't tell me you didn't go to Garden House.
Keith: Why would I go there?
Amber: For Liz's birthday cake! I left you a voice message this morning!
Keith: But you said Matt would go to the bakery! And why did you come here without me? I was waiting outside your apartment for an hour!
Amber: No! I said I'd have lunch with Matt, and we'd come straight here from the restaurant. So I asked you to help get the cake after work.
Keith: No, you did not! And why didn't you answer my calls?
Amber: My cellphone is dead! I said in the message that you could call Matt's number if you wanted to find me. Now please tell me you did bring the gift we got for Liz.
Keith: What gift? I'm sure you didn't say anything about a gift in the message.
Amber: I told you that yesterday!

【104年會考】
e: 由對話中Amber要Keith去拿蛋糕，可推知為麵包店，故選(Ａ)。

p:

He did not know how to get to Amber's apartment.
He called Amber without knowing her phone was not working.
He did not know Amber left him a voice message this morning.
e: 由對話中Amber提到“My phone is dead!”可知Amber的電話壞了，但Keith並不知道，故選(Ｃ)。

s: (３)Which sentence was most likely part of the message that Amber left Keith this morning?
p:
(At Liz's birthday party)
Amber: Don't tell me you didn't go to Garden House.
Keith: Why would I go there?
Amber: For Liz's birthday cake! I left you a voice message this morning!
Keith: But you said Matt would go to the bakery! And why did you come here without me? I was waiting outside your apartment for an hour!

【104年會考】
o: “Matt and I will go to the party after lunch.”
“Don't forget to buy a birthday gift for Liz.”
“You can go straight to the party from your office.”
“I need to talk to you about the party this weekend.”
e:
由對話中Amber提到她跟Keith留言說「我會跟Matt一起吃午餐，然後我們會從餐廳過來這裡。」，故選(Ａ)她和Matt吃完午餐後會直接過去。
中譯：（在Liz的生日派對上）
Amber：別跟我說你沒去Garden House。
Keith：我為什麼要去？
Amber：為了Liz的生日蛋糕！我今早留了個語音留言給你！
Keith：但妳說Matt會去蛋糕店啊！而且妳為何沒跟我一起過來？我在妳的公寓外等了一個小時！
Amber：不！我說我會跟Matt共進午餐，然後我們會從餐廳直接過來這。所以我請你在工作結束後去幫忙拿蛋糕。
Keith：不，妳才沒有！而且妳為何沒接我的電話？
Amber：我的手機壞了！我在留言中說，如果你想要找我，你可以打Matt的電話。現在，拜託你告訴我你有帶我們要給Liz的禮物。
Keith：什麼禮物？我確定妳沒在留言中提到任何有關禮物的事情。
Amber：我昨天就跟你說了！

s: (１)What lesson can we learn from Froggie's story?
p: 【104年會考】
o: Life is too short; one should live it to the fullest.
Those who use their time well will win in the end.
People are blind to problems that slowly get worse over time.
It is difficult to give up old habits, but easy to pick up new ones.
e: 剛開始青蛙遇到熱水的時候，非常警覺地跳出來，然而後來遇到溫水的時候，卻喪失了警覺性，悠哉的洗澡，故選(Ｃ)。

s: (２)What do we know about Froggie?
p: 【104年會考】
o: He learned to share what he liked with others.
He thought what he had hoped for became real.
He once almost lost a dear friend to a water snake.
He wanted to go back to the same pot for a hot bath.
e:
文中第三段提到Froggie覺得這裡就是他夢寐以求的地方了，故選(Ｂ)。
中譯：　　Froggie是隻從來不記得他到過哪裡的青蛙。他最大的夢想是找到最好的池塘，可以讓他自由自在地游泳，而且不用擔心有水蛇。有一天，Froggie跳到一個廚房，然後跳進一鍋熱水當中。Froggie覺得很燙，馬上用他最快的速度跳離水中。「我差點就死在那了！」Froggie想著。
　　幾天後，Froggie回到同樣的廚房裡，完全忘記他來過這裡。他再次跳入了相同的鍋中。這次，在鍋裡的水是冷的。他看了看四周，想著：「這裡沒有會吃我的水蛇，我可以獨享這個地方呢！」就在此時，Froggie知道了這就是他的夢想之地。但他有所不知的是，這鍋水，正用小火慢慢地加熱當中。
　　游了三十分鐘後，Froggie感覺到水變溫暖了，但他把這當成是個驚喜。「這果然是最好的游泳地點，我還可以洗個熱水澡呢。」在他享受熱水澡的過程中，水溫持續的變暖變熱。而Froggie因為太過舒服而睡著了。結果，他就再也沒醒來了。

s: (１)What does it mean when someone is in a calamitous state?
p: 【104年會考】
o: They are looking for a second chance.
They lost interest in the outside world.
e: 整篇文章在描述上教堂的人數減少，教堂收入銳減，有些面臨轉賣以及倒閉的危機，故選(Ａ)。

s: (２)What can we learn about the church-goers from the report?
p: 【104年會考】
o: Between 1980 and 2005, few church-goers were younger than 50.
In 2010, only 6％ of church-goers were younger than 50 years old.
In 2020, the percentage（％）of church-goers drops to lower than half that in 1980.
Between 1980 and 2020, the rising number of old church-goers has led to an old church.
e: 根據圖表一，在2020年上教堂的人數為4.4％，而1980年代上教堂的人數為11％，人數整整少了一半的百分比，故選(Ｃ)。

s: (３)What is talked about in the report?
p: 【104年會考】
o: How people decide to join a church.
What happens to churches that are closed.
Why people have stopped going to church.
e: 文中第二段提到一些幸運的教堂會被轉賣成作為其他用途，而沒那麼幸運的教堂就會倒閉關門大吉，故選(Ｃ)。

s: (４)Below are four findings from other reports.  Which does NOT agree with the idea of the report?
p: 【104年會考】
o: “Reports show over 90％ of church-goers go to church because their fathers do.  In the last 20 years, 49％ of men under 30 have left the church.  That means there's a 90％ chance that their children won't go to church.  This is hard for the church to take in.”
“Between 2003 and 2010, over 1,000 new churches were built in the country.  This may sound like good news.  During the same years, however, more than 2,000 were closed.”
“In the report, 33％ of the people that were interviewed say they never go to church and another 33％ say they used to.  Only 15％ go to church at least once a month.”
“Of the 15 countries in the report, the percentage（％）of church-goers in some countries, like Denmark, is lower than 10％; in others, like Poland, the percentage is higher than 70％.”
e:
選項(Ｄ)波蘭上教堂的人數比高於70％，與文章中圖表一明顯不符合，故選(Ｄ)。
中譯：都會時報
2020年10月1日
　　這些年來，教堂處於一種悲慘的狀態。首先，去教堂的人數劇烈的遞減（見圖表一）。許多人說他們沒有所屬的教堂，而那些會去教堂的人，則是降低了去的次數。去教堂這件事情越來越少出現在人們的待辦事項裡。另一個令人擔憂的事實是，越來越少年輕人去教堂了，導致教堂的高齡化現象（見圖表二）。
　　還有個跟錢有關的問題。維持教堂持續營運並不便宜。越少人去教堂即代表教堂收入也變少。這使得教堂要維持運作更加困難。
　　當教堂面臨關閉的問題時，除了賣掉它之外，沒有太多其他方法。夠幸運的教堂都能找到買主，並將教堂用於其他地方。例如，有些變成了餐廳或是學校體育館，甚至有些變成了夜店。有些沒那麼幸運的教堂最後則是被拆除。
　　就像流失客源的商店般，教堂也需要想其他方法去解決這個問題，讓教堂重新贏得人心，並在人們的生活中再次變得重要。這並不是單靠祈禱就能解決的。
